title: Small sheaf coproducts: local labels, monicity and the empty-cover criterion
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], small in a universe containing its objects and morphisms [def-weil-size-convention], and let $I$ be a small set. Let $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ be sheaves of sets on $\mathcal D$. Define the presheaf $P$ by $P(V)=\coprod_{i\in I}G_i(V)=\{(i,s):i\in I,\ s\in G_i(V)\}$, with label-preserving restriction maps. There exists a sheafification $\eta:P\to C=P^\#$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. With $c_i(s)=\eta(i,s)$, the cofan $(C,(c_i)_i)$ is a coproduct in sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: for every sheaf $H$, precomposition induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(C,H)\simeq\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}(G_i,H)$. Each $c_i$ is injective on every section set and is a monomorphism, meaning that postcomposition with $c_i$ cancels between morphisms of sheaves. Every $a\in C(V)$ has a covering $\{V_\alpha\to V\}_\alpha$ and labelled sections $(i_\alpha,s_\alpha)\in P(V_\alpha)$ whose images are $a|_{V_\alpha}$. If $i\ne j$ and $s\in G_i(V)$, $t\in G_j(V)$ satisfy $c_i(s)=c_j(t)$, then the empty family is a covering of $V$. For every sheaf $H$, $H(V)$ is a singleton whenever the empty family covers $V$. If $I=\varnothing$, then $C(V)$ is a singleton when the empty family covers $V$ and is empty otherwise.

source.place: Tag 00WI (lemma-colimit-sheaves), specialized to small discrete diagrams; Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification) and Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), for local labels and local equality. Agent formulation of the labelled-sum monicity and empty-cover consequences.

proof.text: Construct P as the labelled sigma presheaf. Put K = J.toGrothendieck and C = K.sheafify P, the concrete double-plus sheafification. Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.sheafify_isSheaf proves that C is a sheaf; its toSheafify_sheafifyLift and sheafify_hom_ext prove the required factorization bijection. These APIs work in Type(max u v w), by the usual smallness instances for multiequalizers and covering colimits. Set eta = K.toSheafify P and c_i equal to the label-i inclusion followed by eta.

For a family of sheaf morphisms $f_i:G_i\to H$, define a presheaf morphism $f:P\to H$ by $f_V(i,s)=(f_i)_V(s)$. Naturality is exactly the naturality of the $f_i$, since restrictions preserve labels. Every presheaf map out of $P$ has this form uniquely, by evaluation on each pair $(i,s)$. The universal property of $\eta$ now extends $f$ uniquely to $\bar f:C\to H$ with $\bar f c_i=f_i$. Conversely, these equations determine $f=\bar f\eta$ on every pair and then determine $\bar f$. Thus the specified precomposition map is a bijection and the cofan is a coproduct. This argument also applies when $I$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 00WI (lemma-colimit-sheaves), discrete-diagram case; direct verification of the universal property

proof.text: First prove that every K-covering sieve contains an actual J-covering presieve, by induction on Precoverage.Saturate. Generating covers and the maximal sieve are immediate. In the pullback case index a covering presieve by its actual arrows (a type in max u v); use the pullbacks supplied by IsSiteForCoverings and downward closure of the sieve. In the transitive case choose one refining cover for each distinct covering arrow and use the bind axiom. Next prove local injectivity and local surjectivity of toPlus in the larger value universe from the concrete plus representative and equality APIs, exactly as in Mathlib LocallyInjective and LocallySurjective. Compose these properties for the two plus units. The covering image sieve of eta, refined to an actual J-presieve by the preceding induction, supplies the local labelled representatives.

For two sections of G_i with equal images, local injectivity of eta gives a covering equalizer sieve. The covering-refinement helper supplies an actual J-cover. Equality of pairs with fixed first coordinate implies equality of their second coordinates. Apply the separatedness of G_i for this J-cover to conclude equality of the sections. Mathlib Sheaf.mono_of_injective then gives Mono c_i by sectionwise cancellation.

For distinct labels i and j with equal images, local injectivity of eta and covering refinement give a J-covering presieve R on which the corresponding pairs agree. Applying Sigma.fst on every arrow would give i=j. Thus R has no arrows and equals the bottom presieve, which therefore belongs to J V.

source.place: Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), local equality; Definition 00VH (definition-site) and the project reindexing convention

proof.text: If the bottom presieve covers V, its generated bottom sieve belongs to K V. Mathlib Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover then makes H(V) a terminal type. Types.isTerminalEquivUnique supplies its element and uniqueness, yielding both Nonempty and Subsingleton.

source.place: Definition 00VR (definition-sheaf), equalizer for the empty covering

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, every $P(W)$ is empty. If $a\in C(V)$ existed, step 3 would give a covering $(W_\beta\to V)_{\beta\in B}$ together with $p_\beta\in P(W_\beta)$. There can be no $\beta$, since its $p_\beta$ would belong to the empty set. Hence $B$ is empty and the same reindexing convention shows that the empty family covers $V$. Consequently $C(V)$ is empty whenever the empty family does not cover $V$; when it does cover $V$, step 6 makes $C(V)$ a singleton. These are both cases of the final assertion.

proof_origin.place: Tags 00WB, 00WH, 00WI and 00WK; U3 implementation using Mathlib concrete double-plus sheafification and its universal-property API. Covering refinement is an induction on saturation under the stated covering-presieve axioms. The private larger-universe local-plus proofs generalize the corresponding Mathlib proofs without changing any public statement.

Sources checked in tags/tags and sites.tex: 00WI lemma-colimit-sheaves (lines 2114-2131) and 00WK lemma-sections-sheafification (lines 2156-2175); the cited nodes carry 00WB/00WH. Step by step: step 1 uses clauses (2) and (3) of the plus theorem (P^{++} is a sheaf with the universal property), not the bare definition. Step 2 proves the discrete-colimit Hom bijection by hand, including I empty. Step 3 gets the local labels from the sections-local node. Step 4 gets sectionwise injectivity from local equality plus the G_i equalizer condition, then monicity by evaluating at every section. Step 5: for i != j, local equality forces the covering's index set B to be empty, and the explicit bijective-reindexing convention of def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology turns that into the empty family covering V. Step 6: over an empty covering both products are singletons, so H(V) is a singleton. Step 7: for I empty every P(W) is empty, so any section forces an empty covering; the converse is step 6. Edge cases tested: I empty with and without empty covers, a singleton I, open covers of a topological space, and infinite I. Duplicate search (00WI, coproducts of sheaves, empty family, labelled sum): finite-extensivity and finite-subcoproducts cover finite or topological-space cases only, and nothing else states the item. lean.statement: theorem small_sheaf_coproduct_labels {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] (J : Precoverage D) (hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) {I : Type w} (G : I → Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u v w))) : ∃ (C : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u v w))) (eta : sheafCoproductLabelPresheaf (fun i ↦ (G i).obj) ⟶ C.obj) (c : ∀ i : I, G i ⟶ C), (∀ (i : I) (V : D) (s : (G i).obj.obj (op V)), (c i).hom.app (op V) s = eta.app (op V) ⟨i, s⟩) ∧ (∀ H : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u v w)), Function.Bijective (fun f : C ⟶ H ↦ eta ≫ f.hom)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk C c)) ∧ (∀ H : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u v w)), Function.Bijective (fun f : C ⟶ H ↦ fun i : I ↦ c i ≫ f)) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (V : D), Function.Injective ((c i).hom.app (op V))) ∧ (∀ i : I, Mono (c i)) ∧ (∀ (V : D) (a : C.obj.obj (op V)), ∃ S : Presieve V, S ∈ J V ∧ ∀ (W : D) (f : W ⟶ V), S f → ∃ (i : I) (s : (G i).obj.obj (op W)), eta.app (op W) ⟨i, s⟩ = C.obj.map f.op a) ∧ (∀ (V : D) (i j : I) (s : (G i).obj.obj (op V)) (t : (G j).obj.obj (op V)), i ≠ j → (c i).hom.app (op V) s = (c j).hom.app (op V) t → (⊥ : Presieve V) ∈ J V) ∧ (∀ (H : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u v w))) (V : D), (⊥ : Presieve V) ∈ J V → Nonempty (H.obj.obj (op V)) ∧ Subsingleton (H.obj.obj (op V))) ∧ (IsEmpty I → ∀ V : D, ((⊥ : Presieve V) ∈ J V → Nonempty (C.obj.obj (op V)) ∧ Subsingleton (C.obj.obj (op V))) ∧ ((⊥ : Presieve V) ∉ J V → IsEmpty (C.obj.obj (op V))))
